use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: If the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate (i.e., when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the tracks would decorrelate), the correlation is rejected.
If the C2 JU receives a J7.2 Correlation message while holding Operational Contingency Constraints (OCCs) on both tracks or conflicting IDs, it rejects the correlation.

If a J7.2 message has the RV field set to value 3, the correlation was manually initiated and is automatically accepted unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) different E/C or existing E/C conflict, (2) one simulated and one live track, or (3) both locally derived real-time tracks; in these cases the correlation is rejected.
When the RV field is set to value 0, a reverse correlation would be acceptable; when the RV field is set to value 1, a reverse correlation request is rejected.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN with the RV field set to value 0 and the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint, reverse correlation is transmitted; if both Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation is rejected.
When a correlation request is rejected for manual correlation, the JU originating the request provides an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.

If a J7.0 (ACT=0) message is received, the R² unit is declared inactive; a JU receiving that message on a locally held track assumes R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

If a JU has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds, it assumes R² for that track.
If a JU without R² for a nonreal-time track whose TQ field is set to value 0 locally updates that track with a new nonreal-time report, it assumes R² for the track.

If J2 messages are not received subsequent to this action and the receiving C² JU still has no local data, the C² JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
If a correlation is not found for a received J2 PPLI report, the C² JU integrates the report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.

If the operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the operator has the following manual actions available: update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; initiate J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode); initiate J7.5 (ACT=1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode); change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing assignment of a new track number to local data; or clear the operator alert (any mode).

missing_aspects: Main-flow step-number anchors for these exception branches were not available and should be added during integration with the main_flow.
Post-rejection continuation after automatic correlation rejections is undocumented; only manual-correlation rejection has a documented operator-alert recovery.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU must be in Active status, having either initially achieved Active status or returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
The C2 JU must be capable of assuming R² for air, surface, or land tracks.
A new local track that does not tentatively correlate on the initial correlation test is transmitted.
A new local track that tentatively correlates on the initial test but fails correlation on the next test is transmitted.
If the automatic correlation test fails during execution, the system assigns a new Track Number (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message with an initial ID of Pending.

A new local track that correlates with another track on each of the first two correlation tests is correlated and held as a common local track; thereafter, the decorrelation rules apply to that track.

After successful publication of an Inactive or Limited Status Interface Unit (IU) track, the C² JU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG with Identity reported as Friend, and the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator are reported as value 1 and are maintained if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.
The C2 JU withholds transmission of air/surface tracks until reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed.
The C2 JU automatically correlates real-time air/surface tracks by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.

The C2 JU does not automatically correlate two tracks when local/remote data indicate an Identity conflict, different current Mode II codes, both tracks locally derived real-time, or either track with a Strength field greater than 1.
For each common local track, the C2 JU performs automatic decorrelation tests upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.

When the position or other data in a PPLI meet the decorrelation criteria, including a remote track falling outside 1.5 times the maximum correlation distance on 2 consecutive remote track reports, the C2 JU decorrelates the PPLI and the local track data.
After decorrelation, the C2 JU reports the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field as No Statement.
The C2 JU automatically tests the local track once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks); the automatic correlation test fails.
The C2 JU assigns a new track number (TN B) to the local track.
The C2 JU waits the minimum 12 seconds before reporting the air/surface track.
The C2 JU reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message with an initial ID of Pending, initiating the surveillance track report with locally held data using the new track number.
The C2 JU establishes TN A as a remote track.

The C2 JU is triggered to publish an air or surface track after initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, once sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed for that track.
C2 JU publishes air and surface surveillance tracks to the surveillance network after performing the required reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration.

scope_contract.goal_statement: C2 JU publishes air and surface surveillance tracks to the surveillance network after performing the required reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: One canonical successful instance: the C2 JU, in Active status, publishes a single air or surface surveillance track by transmitting it to the surveillance network after the required reporting responsibility checks, correlation, data registration, and any necessary automatic decorrelation have been performed.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The C2 JU is in Active status and holds an air or surface surveillance track that is ready to be transmitted.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The air or surface surveillance track has been transmitted to the surveillance network.
in_scope_actions: transmit/report the air or surface surveillance track

missing_aspects: The cited evidence cards (EC-TR-000, EC-MF-011) specify that checks must be performed before transmission is allowed, but do not explicitly state that the system 'publishes' the tracks as a resulting action or outcome. Furthermore, while EC-G-001 mandates the capability for automatic decorrelation, it does not support the claim that this capability is applied specifically during the publishing step described in the main flow.
